definition: An in-sample test compares a model's predictions to the same data used to fit the model; an out-of-sample test compares predictions to data the model has not seen.
core_idea: In-sample testing checks how well a model fits the data it was built from, while out-of-sample testing checks whether the model generalizes to new, unseen data.
key_points: The author frames in-sample testing as the initial, more basic check performed first.
Out-of-sample testing is described as a later step, using data not used to build the model.
relationships: Part of the broader error analysis process.
trading_implications: A model that performs well in-sample but poorly out-of-sample is likely overfit and unreliable for forward-looking trading or hedging decisions.
caveats: Good in-sample fit alone does not guarantee a model will predict future, unseen conditions well.
